title: Recognition abroad versus in the United States
summary: They discuss Japan, Freddie Hubbard's complaint and Europe's appreciation of jazz.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. You also mentioned that Dud Bascomb had told you that in Japan, they knew you and they were waiting for you.

Right. That's, I really want to go there. I wanted to go there then. But, I didn't get the opportunity to on account of the work I was doing here. Dud used to, everytime he'd go there, he and Sam Taylor, told me about Japan. They said they knew all about my records, and all those different things about me. They said they know more about you than you know about yourself, especially the people in the States. They said the people don't keep up with you in the States like they do in Europe. You know?
How do you feel about that?

Well, you know, I think I can quite understand the people in the States because they've got you here. They can hear you. They can go here and there and hear you. Over there, you don't get a chance to, they don't get a chance to hear you until you do make your mind to come up. So, they've got the albums, the books, and things, they read about you, and they're very anxious to see you when you get there. You know, when you do get there.
Like I said, I had never been there and they had books, albums, and everything about me out there when I got there.
Right. Cause that's something that's come up with a lot of musicians.

Freddie Hubbard was very angry on Dick Cavett's show, you know, a few years back, because he says when he gets to Paris, they are asking him to do this movie or do this and do that. And he says here I am talking to you, and

you don't even know who I am. You know, and I'm the best trumpet player in the world. And that, and Dizzy. He was on and talking a while back too. He was talking about the same thing. He says well, in the States, they forget about you after awhile, you know, after about two weeks. You know? And, things of that nature. So, whether joking or what, there's really a little tinge of sadness in that too because jazz musicians have always wondered well why is it that I have to go to Europe or Japan to find somebody who thinks enough about my music to think that I'm really doing something great. In that sense, and that's something that we have never really had, an appreciation for the music in the United States. And, it is our only art music.
That's true.
Yeah. And, so it was in that regard I was asking you. How does it feel to get that kind of recognition as soon as you're, you know, in another country?

That's, it was very surprised me at first cause it was my first time over there. But, I heard about it, you know, how they receive you when you get over there. But, I found that to be true, and then I said my, my.

Then, I found it different between there and here. I know that's how Coleman Hawkins and Louis Armstrong actually had to make themselves big. They went and stayed about 10 or 12 years, you know, before they actually got a big name, and then came back.

But that kind of reception, everything that I've read all the way back. I mean all the way back that James Reese Europe went over and Sidney Bechet (inaudible) you know. Ernest Ansermet And his writings, you know, relate to that whole kind of thing there. That's something that I guess that we don't get a chance to get around.
And the fact is, as Dud was saying, you know when he came back, they turn out in Japan by the stadium load. You know, just the same way that they come to a baseball game here
at Shea Stadium. They turn out for jazz in that same way.
Yeah, right. Well. he told me all about it. I said well, maybe, I'll get there one day.
Okay. So, we said, what about that South American tour that they had you down here as flying your family around? Were you looking forward to that one too?
Well, I'm looking forward to it. Sure. I would like to. I like to make them all. That's since I'm flying now. I wasn't flying before, but they say I was flying. Right?
Right? That's right. They had you down there.
I'd like to make it.
